mainTopic: How long a נדר on property lasts ("נכסים אלו" versus "נכסי"), entering a friend's field in שביעית, and a new משנה on business dealings between a מודר הנאה and his friend.
overview: The גמרא finishes a ראיה that a נדר can last after the owner dies. It then pushes the ראיה away, because in that case the father said "בחייו ובמותו" outright. Next it redefines the מחלוקת: with "נכסים אלו" everyone agrees the איסור stays, and the argument is only about "נכסי". A משנה that tells "your house" apart from "this house" challenges רב ושמואל. The גמרא concludes that the two pairs of אמוראים never argued. רב ושמואל spoke about "נכסים אלו", and רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש spoke about "נכסי". The גמרא then asks why a מודר הנאה may not enter his friend's field in שביעית, when the land is open to all. עולא answers that the trees stand on the border, and רבי שמעון בן אליקים answers that it is a גזירה in case he lingers. Finally, a new משנה forbids lending, borrowing, selling and buying between two people bound by a נדר of הנאה.

steps.title: The punchline of the proof: the son does not inherit
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source ends: if the father dies, the son does not inherit him. So the איסור goes on even after the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father dies, the son does not inherit from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it began just before this. The source says that if the father dies, the son still cannot inherit from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After death the property is no longer the father's, yet the son is still forbidden to benefit from it. That looks like proof that a person can forbid his property in a way that lasts even after it leaves his possession.

phrases.english: If he dies — he does not inherit him!
phrases.notes: This is the end of a source quoted just before. A father forbade his son from benefiting from him, so the son can't inherit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun earlier on the daf.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can forbid his property in a way that lasts even after it leaves his possession.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source about a father who forbids his son to benefit from him: if he dies, the son does not inherit.

steps.title: Rejected: that father said "in life and in death"
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. In that case the father said outright that the איסור applies during his life and after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because he told him explicitly: "during his life and upon his death."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. In that case the father spelled out that the נדר covers the time after his death too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור lasted there only because the father said so in words. That tells us nothing about a normal case where the person did not say that the נדר continues after the property leaves him.

keyTerms.meaning: during his life and upon his death

steps.confusionAlert: This דחיה does not say the opposite is true. It only says this source cannot prove anything, because the case had extra wording.

phrases.english: It is different here
since he said to him, "during his life and upon his death."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes away the proof from Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from this source. It proves nothing about a case where the person did not explicitly extend the איסור. Step 3 then returns to a different, earlier question, which Step 4 answers.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source has explicit wording (בחייו ובמותו) that makes it a special case.

steps.title: The first question is still difficult
steps.stepSummary: Even with the proof answered, the earlier question still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is still difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that one problem has been handled, but the earlier question still stands. This line sets up the new explanation of the מחלוקת in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question asked why רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש argued only in a certain way and not also about "נכסים אלו". Rejecting the proof did not answer that, so a new approach is needed.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult?
phrases.notes: He means the first question asked earlier on the daf. The next step answers it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, goes back to the earlier unanswered problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier understanding of the מחלוקת between רב ושמואל and רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier way of reading their dispute still leaves the first question unexplained.

steps.title: New version: everyone agrees about "this property"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא redefines the dispute. With "נכסים אלו" everyone agrees; they argue only about "נכסי".
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: when he said "this property," everyone agrees. They disagree when he said "my property."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by moving the argument to a different case. If he said "this property," nobody argues; the argument is only about "my property."
steps.deeperAnalysis: "נכסים אלו" points at specific things, so the איסור sticks to the objects themselves wherever they go. "נכסי" might mean "whatever belongs to me," so once it is no longer his, perhaps the איסור ends. That is where the argument now lies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the key difference in the sugya: a נדר on a specific object versus a נדר on "what is mine."

phrases.english: Rather: with "this property" —
everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: They all agree the איסור stays even after the property leaves his hands.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is with "my property."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בִּ״נְכָסִים אֵלּוּ״ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in Step 3 by redefining the case of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the dispute (אלא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about a case where the איסור continues after the property leaves him, apparently including "נכסים אלו".
steps.terutzMaskana: With "נכסים אלו" everyone agrees the איסור stays; the dispute is only about "נכסי".

steps.title: The two sides of the dispute, spelled out
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל: the איסור stays in both cases. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש: it stays with "נכסים" but not with "נכסי".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל hold: there is no difference between "this property" and "my property"; either way a person can forbid it. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש hold: with "property" a person can forbid it, but with "my property" he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out each side of the new version of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל say both wordings forbid the property even after it leaves him. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש say the word "my" limits the נדר to the time it belongs to him. Once he sells it or dies, the איסור is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: a person can forbid (and it stays forbidden)

steps.whatToRemember: With "נכסים אלו" everyone agrees the איסור stays. With "נכסי", רב ושמואל say it stays, and רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש say it ends once the property is no longer his.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel hold:
no difference "this property," no difference "my property,"
a person forbids.
phrases.notes: He means the איסור keeps working even after the property is sold or the owner dies.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish hold:
"property" — a person forbids,
"my property" — a person does not forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the positions within the new framing given in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ושמואל: the איסור stays with both "נכסים אלו" and "נכסי". רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש: it stays only with "נכסים", not with "נכסי".

steps.title: Challenge to רב ושמואל from the משנה about "your house" and "this house"
steps.stepSummary: Can anyone really say there is no difference? A משנה rules that "your house" becomes מותר after a sale or death, while "this house" stays אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anyone who says it makes no difference between "this property" and "my property"? But we learned in a משנה: If one says to his friend, "Entering your house is קונם for me," or "buying your field is קונם for me," and the owner died or sold it to another, it is permitted. If he said "this house that I enter" or "this field that I buy," and the owner died or sold it to another, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ושמואל with a משנה. That משנה clearly treats "your" property differently from "this" property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, "your house" works like "נכסי" because it ties the נדר to the owner, and it ends once the owner sells or dies. "This house" works like "נכסים אלו" and stays אסור. That fits רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש and seems to go against רב ושמואל, who said there is no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: a word used to make a נדר, like "forbidden like a קרבן"
he sold it to someone else

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, the person who made the נדר is forbidding himself from his friend's house. Still, the same difference applies: "your" ties the נדר to the owner, while "this" ties it to the object.

phrases.english: And is there anyone who says
no difference "this property" and no difference "my property"?
But didn't we learn:
One who says to his friend
"Konam that I enter into your house,"
"your field that I buy,"
if he died or sold it to another — permitted.
phrases.notes: "He" is the owner. Once the house or field isn't "yours" anymore, the נדר no longer applies.

phrases.english: "this house that I enter,"
"this field that I buy,"
if he died or sold it to another — forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the position of רב ושמואל as spelled out in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position of רב ושמואל that there is no difference between "נכסים אלו" and "נכסי".
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה clearly separates "your house/field" (מותר after a sale or death) from "this house/field" (still אסור). That shows wording tied to ownership makes a difference.

steps.title: The two pairs of אמוראים never actually argued
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how it reads the two opinions. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש were talking about "נכסי", and רב ושמואל were talking about "נכסים אלו". So there is no dispute at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: when רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש said the איסור goes away, they meant a case where he said "my property". When רב ושמואל said it stays, they meant a case where he said "this property". They do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. It explains that each pair of אמוראים was talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked how רב ושמואל could ignore the משנה's difference between "your house" and "this house". The answer is that they did not ignore it. רב ושמואל only spoke about "נכסים אלו", where the איסור really does stay. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש only spoke about "נכסי", where it goes away, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier reading is being dropped for a new one
"My property": wording tied to the owner, so it stops once the item leaves him
"This property": wording tied to the items themselves, so the איסור stays with them

steps.whatToRemember: "נכסי" (my property) means the איסור ends once the item is sold or the owner dies. "נכסים אלו" (this property) means the איסור stays. Everyone agrees on both.

phrases.english: Rather: when they said
Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, it was about "my property".
phrases.notes: He means their ruling that the איסור goes away. That ruling was only about the wording "my property".

phrases.english: And Rav and Shmuel, it was about "this property",
and they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כִּי אָמְרִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by placing each opinion in a different case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each pair of אמוראים addressed a different wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל held the איסור stays even with "נכסי", which goes against the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ושמואל spoke only of "נכסים אלו", and רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש spoke only of "נכסי". They agree.

steps.title: In שביעית the land is open to all, so why can't he enter the field?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in שביעית he may not enter the field but may eat fruit that leans out of it. It asks why. If he may eat because the fruit is הפקר, the land is also opened to everyone in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "In שביעית he may not go down into his field" and so on. What is different that he may eat from the fruit that leans out? Because the fruit is ownerless. But the Torah made the land ownerless too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier משנה about a מודר הנאה and his friend's field. It challenges the rule for שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets him eat the leaning fruit in שביעית because that fruit belongs to no one, so he gets no הנאה from his friend. But in שביעית everyone is allowed to walk into fields to eat. So entering the land should not count as benefit from the owner either. Why, then, does the משנה forbid entering?

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year (שמיטה), when produce is ownerless
Fruit hanging or leaning out beyond the field
Ownerless; free for anyone to take

phrases.aramaic: וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית אֵין יוֹרֵד לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "And in the Sabbatical Year he may not go down into his field," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the earlier משנה. The rest of it says he may still eat from the fruit that leans out.

phrases.english: What is different that he may eat from the leaning fruit?
Because they are ownerless fruit,
the land too, He made it ownerless!
phrases.notes: "He" is the Torah: in שביעית everyone may enter fields to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the נכסי discussion and returns to a later clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that in שביעית he may not enter the field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows the leaning fruit because it is הפקר. But in שביעית the land is also open to all, so entering should be allowed too.

steps.title: עולא: the trees stand on the border
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the משנה is talking about trees on the edge of the field. He can eat without going in, so entering is not needed and stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: the case is where the trees stand on the borders of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trees are on the border, he can pick the fruit from outside. The Torah only opened fields so people could reach the fruit. Here he has no need to walk in, so stepping on his friend's land would be forbidden הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Borders or edges of the field

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is where the trees stand on the borders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: בְּעוֹמְדִין אִילָנוֹת עַל הַגְּבוּלִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the trees are on the edge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah opened all fields in שביעית, entering his friend's field should be allowed, so the משנה's ban on entering seems to have no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can reach the fruit from outside, so entering is unnecessary and forbidden

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אליקים: a decree in case he lingers
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים gives a different answer. Even when the trees are inside the field, the rabbis made a גזירה against entering, because he might stand around longer than he needs to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אליקים said: it is a rabbinic decree, in case he remains standing there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. Here the משנה applies even when the trees are in the middle of the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah opens the field only for eating its fruit. Lingering there is benefit from the owner's land, and that is not הפקר. To keep him from lingering, the rabbis forbade entering altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to keep people from a real איסור

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said:
It is a decree, lest he remain standing there.
phrases.notes: Standing around longer than needed for eating is benefit from his friend's land, which is still forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁהֶא בַּעֲמִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 8, different from עולא's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the land is open in שביעית, entering should be fully allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: Entering is forbidden by גזירה, in case he lingers beyond what eating needs
steps.whyThisMatters: עולא's answer only covers trees on the border. This answer forbids entering even when the trees are inside the field.

steps.title: New משנה: no lending, borrowing, selling or buying
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that when one person is forbidden by נדר from benefiting from another, the two may not lend or borrow items, may not lend or borrow money, and may not sell to or buy from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is forbidden by vow from benefit from his friend: he may not lend him an item or borrow one from him, may not lend him money or borrow money from him, and may not sell to him or buy from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists business dealings that are forbidden between two people when a נדר of הנאה is in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of actions works in both directions, because each one gives some benefit to one side. Borrowing an item, getting a loan, or making a sale all bring a benefit, so a נדר of הנאה blocks all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: One forbidden by vow from getting benefit
Lend him an object (to be returned itself)
Lend him money (to be paid back with other money)

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר of הנאה blocks lending, borrowing, selling and buying in both directions.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who is forbidden by vow from benefit from his friend:
he may not lend him, nor borrow from him,
phrases.notes: This pair is about lending an object, like a tool, that is given back as is.

phrases.english: he may not loan to him, nor take a loan from him,
phrases.notes: This pair is about lending money.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִמְכּוֹר לוֹ וְלֹא יִקַּח מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: and he may not sell to him, nor buy from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the שביעית discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between two people with a נדר of הנאה, lending and borrowing items or money, and selling and buying, are all forbidden in both directions.
